status: DRAFT — companion to draft-krausz-verification-state-01 v0.4 rev-1.8 (PR #5) — anchors publication rule (root-caused divergence)

vector_keying_rules._note: Design ruling for how conformance vectors are keyed, deduplicated, and integrity-checked. Applies to accept_vectors[], reject_vectors[], and status_vectors[].
vector_keying_rules.primary_key: id — vectors key on id, not envelope_sha256. Two vectors with different ids may share the same envelope (see intentional_collisions below).
vector_keying_rules.envelope_sha256: sha256 of the composed envelope JSON as distributed on disk. Same envelope bytes across separability-family vectors will share the same envelope_sha256; this is by design, not a duplicate.

vector_sha256._note: Distribution-integrity checksum for a vector as a whole. Unique per vector even when envelopes collide (see intentional_collisions).
vector_sha256.construction: sha256 over the JCS-canonical serialization of the following wrapper object:

field_semantics.envelope_sha256: sha256 hex of the composed envelope JSON as distributed on disk — envelope is bound BY HASH here, not by value
field_semantics.anchors: the anchors[] array as it appears in the vector entry
field_semantics.expected_core_validity: boolean — present only on vectors that assert this axis
field_semantics.expected_failure_reason: canonical reject enum string — present only on reject_vectors[]
field_semantics.expected_anchor_status: canonical status enum string — present only on status_vectors[]

vector_sha256.envelope_binding_rationale: The envelope is referenced BY HASH (envelope_sha256), NOT by embedding its bytes inside the wrapper. Rationale: embedding pretty-printed envelope bytes inside a JCS wrapper would create two byte-forms of the envelope (the pretty-printed on-disk copy and the JCS-normalized in-wrapper copy) with different sha256 values, breaking the hash-chain property. Binding by hash means any envelope change ripples through envelope_sha256 into vector_sha256 with a single well-defined dependency.
vector_sha256.omission_rule: Absent expected_* fields MUST be OMITTED from the wrapper before JCS serialization, NEVER set to null. This is §4.1 (null_field_present is a reject in the wire format) applied to the manifest itself — the wrapper obeys the same null-vs-absent discipline as the envelopes it references.
vector_sha256.ingestion: Verifiers SHOULD recompute vector_sha256 during suite ingestion; mismatches indicate the vector was mutated in transit, the wrapper construction disagrees with this spec, OR the manifest is missing per-vector adjudication inputs (see anchors_publication_rule).
vector_sha256.reference_implementation: Both verify.mjs and verify.py MUST implement this construction identically. Composite check output MUST report vector_sha256 per vector alongside the byte-identity assertion across the three separability-family envelopes.

anchors_publication_rule._note: Manifest is the single published home of adjudication inputs. Nothing a conformance runner needs to reproduce vector_sha256 may live off-tree.
anchors_publication_rule.status_vectors_MUST_carry_anchors_verbat: status_vectors[] entries MUST include an `anchors` field carrying the anchors verbatim as they were presented to the adjudicator when the declared vector_sha256 was computed. Because status envelopes are byte-identical to their accept-vector baseline by design (§6 separability made executable), the anchors are the ONLY per-vector adjudication input that distinguishes them — they cannot be reconstructed from the envelope bytes alone.
anchors_publication_rule.accept_and_reject_vectors_OMIT_anchors: accept_vectors[] and reject_vectors[] entries MUST OMIT the `anchors` field. Not [], not null — absent. Their expected outcome is fully determined by the envelope + expected_* fields; no adjudication input beyond that exists. This is §4.1 (null_field_present is a reject in the wire format) applied to the manifest itself.
anchors_publication_rule.why_reject_wrappers_already_matched: The rev-1.5 vector_sha256 recompute matched declared values on reject vectors byte-for-byte because the reject wrapper has no `anchors` field to disagree about — anchors is omitted from both the published entry and any reasonable reconstruction. Status wrappers diverged because Pote's generator included anchors[] content that was never published to the tree; the reconstruction was correct against the published entries, but the entries were incomplete.

intentional_collisions._note: Envelope_sha256 collisions between the following three vectors are INTENTIONAL. The composite check MUST assert the three envelopes are byte-identical — this is separability made executable (same envelope, three different adjudication outcomes depending on anchor state and clock skew).
vectors: v04-accept-001 (baseline: core valid, anchoring meets_commitment, no clock skew)
v04-status-test_clock_in_production (same envelope; core valid; test-clock header flagged as production violation; anchor status independent)
v04-status-skewed_clock_adjudication (same envelope; core valid; verifier-clock skew triggers indeterminate_pending anchor status; core validity preserved per §6 separability rule)

vector_keying_rules.why: Separability of core validity from anchor status (§6 clarifying sentence, rev-1.3) is a spec claim. Making three vectors carry byte-identical envelopes but yield three different adjudication outcomes turns the claim into an executable property: if a verifier folds anchor status into core reject, the three vectors will not all pass their respective expected_* fields. The suite tests the property directly.

accept_vectors.description: First v0.4 accept vector — ratified baseline from PR #5 discussion; AO+AT composed envelope with all v0.4 field groups (evidence, evidence_seals, seals_complete, anchor_commitments) per rev-1.2 pins P-13..18. AT leg hand-signed by @poteshniy from AgentTrust; byte-matched deterministically by build_accept_001.py via the fixture-suite seed convention. Three canonicalizations (RFC 7515 header b64u, RFC 8785 JCS payload, compact-JSON protected header) and two independent signature verifications behind it.
notes: Baseline converged byte-identical 2026-07-29 PM between Claude's Python and Pote's Node implementations (payload = 1823 bytes, sha256 begins 0664f60e…).

AT signature fWTMae9shEBnV_EqWSCSzFfHXxRPfj3bnIyEcCp_sctOzkOL5yQXiEpLRtcfW1dK4qbn13svlDGwkB4jXM6xCg hand-signed by AgentTrust from the seed-derived at-fixture key; verified byte-identical by build_accept_001.py's deterministic regeneration path (Ed25519 is deterministic over the same seed + signing input).

reject_vectors.description: v0.4 field groups present but AT leg protected header declares v0.3 typ. Per §5 content-driven check-set selection, a v0.3-declared envelope carrying v0.4 fields MUST be rejected.
Optional field content_length serialized as null instead of omitted. §4.1: optional fields MUST be omitted, never null.
evidence_seals not ordered lexicographically by ref. §2.5: entries MUST be ordered lexicographically by ref (byte-wise UTF-8).

status_vectors.notes: Same envelope as accept-001. test-clock anchor presented to a production verifier: core validity preserved, anchor status resolves indeterminate_pending. Verifiers MUST NOT fold into core reject (§6 separability).
anchor_commitments min_count=2 over [test-clock, evm-tx], one verified anchor present, past anchor_by → short_of_commitment; core valid, reported alongside not folded (§3.5).

Same envelope as accept-001. Verifier-clock skew: adjudication uses proof-derived test-clock reading, not verifier wall-clock; resolves indeterminate_pending. Core validity preserved (§6 separability).

status_vectors_schema._note: STATUS-domain conformance vectors per §6: core validity holds; adjudication follows §3.5 vocabulary. Verifiers MUST NOT fold anchoring status into core reject. Populated in rev-1.3+ conformance suite. Keying and integrity rules per vector_keying_rules (above).

fields.id: stable identifier, e.g. v04-status-commitment-shortfall-001. PRIMARY KEY.
fields.envelope_file: relative path to signed envelope JSON. May be shared across separability-family vectors (intentional envelope_sha256 collisions per vector_keying_rules).
fields.envelope_sha256: sha256 of the composed envelope JSON. May collide across separability-family vectors by design.
fields.vector_sha256: sha256 over the JCS-canonical full wrapper (envelope + anchors[] + conformance_mode + expected fields). Distribution-integrity checksum; unique per vector even when envelopes collide.
fields.conformance_mode: one of: strict | permissive | test_clock_in_production | skewed_clock_adjudication — the adjudication context under which this vector is tested.
fields.expected_core_validity: boolean — does the composed envelope pass core validity (signatures/canonicalization/seals)?
fields.expected_anchor_status: one of: meets_commitment | short_of_commitment | not_yet_anchored | indeterminate_pending
fields.signer_kids: list[str] — JWKS kids that signed the envelope, in composition order
fields.notes: human-readable disposition and adjudication reference to §3.5
